metaDescription: Build a depreciation schedule from cost, residual value and life using straight-line, declining balance or sum-of-the-years-digits.
intro: Yearly depreciation, accumulated depreciation and book value.
why:
Depreciation spreads the cost of an asset over its life. Straight-line is even, declining balance front-loads, and sum-of-years-digits front-loads less sharply.

The schedule never goes below residual value and uses whole years. Tax rules may require different methods or rates.
howTo: Enter cost, residual value and life.

faq.a: Declining balance uses factor divided by life as the yearly rate. 2 means double declining.
